meta.title: Where Is the Salad?
meta.textType: story: a chant with repeated lines

paragraphs: On Saturday, Tom and Lily made lunch for Grandpa. Tom took the tomatoes and the carrots. They are good vegetables for a salad. Lily put them in a big green bowl. Grandpa liked salad with a lot of sauce. "A good salad needs a good sauce," said Tom. "Let's wash our hands first," said Lily. Pip sat on the kitchen floor, and Squeaky the mouse watched from the window.

The children came back to the table. There was nothing on it! "Where is our salad?" asked Tom. "Did Pip eat it?" asked Lily. "Don't be mean to Pip," said Tom. "Look at him. He has nothing in his mouth." "Let's make a chant," said Lily. "Look down, look down!" "Look back, look back!" "Where is the salad? Where is the salad?" They said it again and again. Tom looked down under the table, and Lily looked back behind the door. Pip said, "Woof, woof!" Squeaky said, "Squeak, squeak!" from the window.

Mom came back into the kitchen. "What are you doing?" she asked. "We can't find the salad," said Lily. Mom laughed. "It's a hot day, so I put it in the fridge," she said. The children opened the fridge. The bowl was at the back, next to the sauce. "Look back, look back!" said Tom, and he smiled. Squeaky got a little carrot. Pip got one too. Then Grandpa came, and the family ate a good lunch.
text.summary: Tom and Lily make a salad for Grandpa, but the bowl is gone. They make a chant and look for it, and Mom shows them that it is in the fridge.
